identity.name: Cascadian First Peoples Hunter
identity.concept: An individual First Peoples hunter defending a Cascadian route, skilled with a recurved bow and able to use Resonance to stir nearby wildlife without summoning creatures.
identity.description: A wary Cascadian route defender who uses cover, a recurved bow, and subtle Resonance with nearby wildlife to pressure intruders while leaving room for withdrawal or conversation.

design.encounterPurpose: A tense, mobile Tier 2 ranged encounter in which violence is possible but not inevitable; the hunter defends a route rather than representing any specific nation or universal First Peoples tradition.
motivesAndTactics: demand intruders stop or turn back
use nearby wildlife to disrupt pursuit
design.designerNotes: Mechanics and Fast Play were approved by the GM before packaging. The character is intentionally not assigned to a specific nation, and the encounter does not present their conduct as universal First Peoples tradition.

prompts.label: Opening
prompts.text: Open from cover and demand that intruders stop or turn back.

prompts.label: Pressure
prompts.text: Press advancing targets with the Recurved Bow and use Press the Shot when one breaks cover.

prompts.label: Wildlife
prompts.text: Use Resonant Wildlife against a pursuer or someone threatening the hunter’s position.

prompts.label: Off-Ramp
prompts.text: Permit withdrawal or conversation when the intruders stop pressing the route.

fastPlay.goal: Create a tense, mobile encounter where violence is not inevitable.

features.name: Trailwise
features.rules: The hunter has advantage on rolls to track creatures or detect movement through familiar wilderness.

features.name: Press the Shot
features.rules: Once per GM turn, when a target within Far range leaves cover, mark 1 Stress to make a standard Recurved Bow attack against them.

features.name: Resonant Wildlife
features.rules: Once per scene, mark 1 Stress to call nearby wildlife around a target within Far range. They make an Instinct Reaction Roll (14). On a failure, they mark 1 Stress and have disadvantage on their next attack against the hunter before the end of the hunter’s next spotlight. On a success, the animals scatter without mechanical effect. If that attack does not occur by the deadline, the disadvantage ends. This uses wildlife already present; it does not summon an Actor.
